New Strategic Initiative: Anchor in Rhode Island Scholarship 15 We propose: • A state-funded matching merit scholarship that doubles URI’s top merit award (up to $12,000/year, $48,000 over 4 years). It helps us: • Retain Rhode Island’s best and brightest high school graduates who might otherwise leave for out-of-state institutions. • Directly support the Governor’s RI2030 priorities: improving education outcomes, raising incomes, and building a stronger workforce. • Strengthen the state’s talent pipeline at a critical time. Expected impact: • Retention of 250+ additional top students annually, enhancing the future workforce and economic competitiveness of the state.

FTE Cap - Requested Increase • URI has a general FTE cap (currently 2,292) and a “third party” FTE cap (currently 379) for positions funded through research. Our total FTE cap is currently 2,671. • In FY25, URI exceeded its then overall FTE cap of 2,571. During the 2025 legislative session, URI requested a 25% increase to the cap (+642). URI is thankful for the +100 FTE increase provided by the General Assembly. • URI is requesting a 20% increase in our overall FTE cap in FY27 (+542 FTEs) to reach the FY26 ask amount, and to reflect enrollment growth, increased research funding (R1), and increased State investment in URI (operating and capital). • Since we were already over the cap in FY25, URI is again at risk of exceeding the cap in FY26. 16

URI Staffing vs. Growth: Why More FTEs Are Essential • Growth outpaces staffing: Student enrollment grew 19% from FY06–FY26, while the FTE cap grew only 4%. • Flat staffing during expansion: From FY19–FY24, URI added ~100 students, $30M in annual research, and a new Board of Trustees with expanded responsibilities — yet the FTE cap stayed flat. • Structural inequity: Research-funded positions have a carve-out, but auxiliary positions (housing, dining, 20–25% of FTEs) do not — despite being self- supported by fees. • Competitive disadvantage: URI is well below peer R1 universities in staffing for HR, IT, facilities, research administration, marketing, and legal. This undercuts student support, research competitiveness, and economic impact. 17

URI’s People Power Drives RI2030 18 Education Outcomes: More faculty/advisors → stronger retention, graduation rates. Income Growth: Career services and industry partnerships connect students to high- wage jobs. Workforce Development: Competitive staffing retains RI’s best students and attracts talent. Economic Growth: Each new FTE is a job in Rhode Island, strengthening the state economy.

Background: In late 2022, the University of Rhode Island engaged a planning team led by Scion Advisory Services, with architects from CannonDesign, to develop a Housing and Residential Life Housing Master Plan to transform URI housing.

This initiative aligned with URI’s strateg ic commitment to enhance t he student experience by providing modern, affordable, and desirable livin g spaces.
The plan recommended that URI pursue a public-private-partnership (P3) to address immediate housing needs on the Kingston campus.
In May 2024, URI issued a public request for proposal for a development partner, and after a thorough vetting process, selected Gilbane Development Company (Gilbane) as its P3 partner.
In September 2024, the University entered into a Preliminary Development Agreement (PDA) with Gilbane.
In March 2025, the University approved the feasibility study conducted by Gilbane confirming that the project was feasible and would move forward.
Gilbane then selected, with URI’s concurrence, Provident to serve as the project 501(c)(3) partner.
PRG – RI Properties LLC, a single member limited liability company, was organized by Provident for the Project.
URI DevCo LLC, a single purpose subsidiary of Gilbane, was also organized for development of the Project.

In April 2025, URI DevCo, Provident, and Raymond James (underwriter) commenced the application process to issue debt through the Rhode Island Health and Education Building Corporation (RIHEBC).
The Project is summarized below.
Project Overview: Project Scope & Design: x Total Beds: 1,134 x Planned Housing Phases: o Occupancy in Fall 2027: 514 undergraduate beds o Occupancy in Fall 2028: 400 undergraduate beds o Occupancy in Fall 2028: 220 graduate beds

x Building Types: o Undergraduate Housing (Two Buildings): Apartment-style, single bedrooms in two- and four- bedroom units.
Modular construction. o Graduate Housing (Six Buildings + Community Center): Apartments with studio, one-bedroom, two-bedroom, and three-bedroom configurations.
Modular rebuild on existing foundations. o All buildings meet state code and URI design standards.
Financial Summary (rounded): x Total Project Cost: $231MM (as of June 2025). x URI Equity Contribution: The University may fund an equity contribution to the Project, the amount of which is currently subject to negotiation, and will be up to the amount authorized by the Board during executive session. x Rental Rates: Rental rates are within acceptable range to URI Housing and Residential Life, though may need to increase due to changes in market conditions. x Annual Rate Escalation: 3% x Expected Occupancy Rate: 95% x Debt Term: 40 years (all-in). x Debt Coverage Ratio: 1.2x or better (Senior Debt). x Residual Cash Flow to URI: $317MM over the term (NPV @ 5% = $63.7MM).

Document Approval Over the past several months, the University has negotiated and vetted several Project documents, three of which are being brought to the Board today for approval, and two of which are being shared for informational purposes.

These documents, listed below, are described in more detail in the enclosed Board of Trustees resolutions. x The Ground Lease between the University and the Provident, will extend for a term of up to 42 years and will contain provisions requiring the Project to be constructed in accordance with campus standards (for approval). x The Affiliation Agreement between the University and Provident, which outlines each entity’s obligations to the project (for approval). x The Interim Management Agreement between the University and URI DevCo LLC, which will allow the University to continue to manage the graduate student housing until the expected turnover date of May 2026, at which time it will be turned over to th e Developer for demolition and re-construction (for approval). x The Turnkey Development Agreement between URI DevCo LLC and Provident, pursuant to which the Developer will implement the design, construction, and commissioning of the Project for a stipulated sum in accordance with plans approved by the University (for information). x The Project Management Agreement between Provident and In wood Management, outlining operations and maintenance of the Student Housing Facilities (for information).

Next Steps Upon the Board’s approval of the Project and authorization to continue negotiating required documents, URI will finalize the negotiation and execute the relevant documents.

Public-Private Partnership Project Summary and Scope The Project is structured as a concession agreement with a private qualified development firm to enter into a public-private partnership (“ P3”), which requires a ground lease for the structure and the issuance of bonds by the Rhode Island Health and Educational Building Corporation (the “ Issuer”).
This P3 is a delivery approa ch, whereby, when appropriate and feasible, the University can utilize the P3 model to secure the anticipated advantages of increased speed of delivery, guaranteed maximum price and firm delivery date, and sh aring risk with the private sector.
In a P3 model, the University leases its land to a tax-exempt nonprofit entity in the form of a ground lease.
That entity engages the developer and contractors to construct the buildings.
The nonprofit entity owns the buildings until the debt is retired.
At that time, ownership reverts to the University, and the ground lease terminates.
Development Process In support of this Project planning, the University solicited proposals on April 30, 2024 for the development and construction of the Student Housing Facilities.

As a result of the solicitation process, Gilbane Development Company, a Rhode Island corporation, was chosen as the lead developer to implement the development financing, construction, equipping, and operation of the

3 4900-8991-3674.4 Project.
URI DevCo LLC, a single purpose subsid iary of Gilbane Development Company, was organized by Gilbane Development Company for development of the Project (the “Developer”).
As a part of the team, Provident Resourc es Group, Inc., a nonprofit 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization established to assist colleges and universities across the country in providing academic and related facilities for their students and otherwise furthering their education missions, (“Provident”) will serve as the tax-exempt parent and sole member of the ground lessee and owner of the facilities, PRG – RI Properties LLC, a si ngle member limited liab ility company (the “Lessee/Borrower”).
The Lessee/Borrower will be organized exclusively to carry out the Project and is not expected to have any assets other than those that are associated with the Project.
The selected team includes Gilban e Building Company, a Rhode Isla nd corporation, as the general contractor and Raymond James as the underwriter.
The architecture partner is CannonDesign.
Inwood Management will perform operations and maintenance of the Student Housing Facilities.

Following the award to the Developer, the University for itself and on behalf of the Board entered into a preliminary development agreement with the Developer to conduct pre-development and design activities for the Project as a whole before bond issuance and closing, currently targeted for September 1, 2025, which date may be subject to change.
The entire process that led to the award of this transaction was reviewed and approved by the Rhode Island Division of Purchases through the URI Office of Strategic Procurement.
Project Structure, Financing and Document Package The total cost of the Project is currently estimated to be approximately $231M, which is expected to be financed through the bond issuance by the Issuer.
The proceeds of the bonds will be loaned by the Issuer to the Lessee/Borrower.
The University may also fund an equity contribution, the amount of which is currently subject to negotiation and will be up to the amount authorized by the Board during executive session.
The proposed financing structure for the Project will be based on a privatized P3 financing model through which the Board will ground lease the land on which the Project is located to the Lessee/Borrower.

The Ground Lease for the Project between the University and the Lessee/Borrower (the “Ground Lease”) will extend for a term of up to 42 years, which will be in excess of the maturity of the proposed bond financing, and will contain provisions requiring the Project to be constructed in accordance with campus standards.
Provisions in the Ground Lease and Affiliation Agreement will also include certain areas of support and c ooperation between the University and the Lessee/Borrower.
Under the Ground Lease, the land will always remain owned by the University, and the Lessee/Borrower will own the Student Housing Facilities for the term of the financing.
Annual rent to the Univ ersity will be Net Available Cash Flow from the Project, estimated over the life of the lease to be a pproximately $317,157,460.
A copy of the form of the Ground Lease, subject to further negotiation and execution as described herein, is attached hereto.

The University and th e Lessee/Borrower w ill also enter into an affiliation agreement (“Affiliation Agreement”) to provide for the University’s obligations with respect to the Project, including the leasing of the Undergraduate Housing Project consistent with its leasing of other on- campus undergraduate student housing.
A copy of the form of the Affiliation Agreement, subject to further negotiation and execution as described herein, is attached hereto.

4 4900-8991-3674.4 The Graduate Student Housing Facility will be turned over to the Developer for demolition and reconstruction after the end of the 2025-2026 academic year.
During the period between closing and turnover, the University will continue to manage the existing graduate village housing consistent with existing management practices pursuant to an interim management agreement (the “Interim Management Agreement”).
A copy of the form of Interim Management Agreement, subject to further negotiation and execution as described herein, is attached hereto.
The Developer and the Lessee/Borrower will enter into a turnkey development agreement (the “Turnkey Development Agreement”) pursuant to which the Developer will implement the design, construction, and commissioning of the Project for a stipulated sum in accordance with plans approved by the University.
The Turnkey Development Agreement is expected to be in substantially the form attached hereto.

Pursuant to the Management Agreem ent between Lessee/Borrower and Inwood Management (the “Management Agreement”), Inwood Management will perform operations and maintenance of the Student Housing Facilities, including all leasing and management of the Graduate Student Housing Facility, in accordance with the Responsibility Matrix attached to the Management Agreement.
The Management Agreement is expected to be in substantially the form attached hereto.
